text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 31 in history:
1433 - Pope Eugenius IV crowned Sigismund as Holy Roman Emperor.
1594 - Tintoretto, born as Jacopo Robusti, a child prodigy and a great Italian artist, died. Among his most famous works are "The Last Judgement" and "The Last Supper".
1669 - Due to failing eyesight, the British admiralty official and diarist Samuel Pepys stopped writing his diary.
1740 - Frederick William I, king of Prussia, died after tranforming his country into a prosperous and powerful one. He was succeeded by his son, Frederick II the Great.
1793 - In France, three days of insurrection and revolt began, leading to the fall of the Girondists from the Convention.
1809 - Franz Josef Haydn, Austrian composer, died. During his 77 years he composed over 100 symphonies, several masses, a series of string quartets and many stage works.
1821 - The Cathedral of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary In Baltimore became the first catholic cathedral to be dedicated in the United States.
1837 - Joseph Grimaldi, famed English dancer and actor whose white-faced act marked the birth of the English circus clown, died.
1859 - Big Ben, the clock tower of the Houses of Parliament in London, began telling the time.
1900 - In the Boer War, the British seized Johannesburg.
1902 - The Treaty of Vereeniging was signed in Pretoria bringing an end to the Boer War. 5,774 British troops and at least 4,000 Boers were killed in action.
1910 - The former British self-governing colonies of Natal, the Transvaal and Cape of Good Hope joined together and formed the Union of South Africa.
1911 - In Belfast, the White Star liner the Titanic was launched as one of the largest vessels afloat. It sank on its maiden voyage in April 1912.
1916 - In World War One, the British blockade of Germany forced the Germans to attack the British Grand Fleet at the indecisive battle of Jutland.
1919 - Lt Cdr A.C. Read and his crew in their Navy-Curtiss flying boat NC-4 completed the first transatlantic flight from Newfoundland to Plymouth. The total flying time was 57 hours 16 minutes.
1923 - Prince Rainier III of Monaco was born. He transformed Monaco from a gambling paradise into a booming international business centre.

1930 - Clint Eastwood, U.S. film star, born. He came to fame in the television series "Rawhide" and then with spaghetti westerns. He also starred as "Dirty Harry". He has directed many films, notably "The Outlaw Josey Wales" and "Unforgiven".
1961 - South Africa proclaimed itself a republic and left the Commonwealth.
1962 - Adolph Eichmann, who helped to organised Nazi Germany's Holocaust murder of millions of Jews, was hanged in Jerusalem.
1994 - Bosnia's parliament elected Croat war veteran Kresimir Zubak as the first interim president of a new power-sharing Moslem-Croat federation.
1996 - Timothy Leary, the counterculture guru of the 1960s who urged a generation of Americans to use the drug LSD so they could "turn on, tune in and drop out", died of cancer.
